patterns.name: Two Pointers
patterns.description: Walk two indices through a sequence (from both ends or at different speeds) to compare or rearrange elements in linear time without extra space.

patterns.name: Fast and Slow Pointers
patterns.description: Advance one pointer twice as fast as another to detect cycles, find midpoints, or locate the start of a loop.

patterns.name: Sliding Window
patterns.description: Maintain a contiguous window that grows and shrinks as you scan, updating a running summary instead of recomputing it.

patterns.name: Intervals
patterns.description: Sort ranges by their start and sweep through them to merge, insert, or intersect overlapping intervals.

patterns.name: In-Place Manipulation of a Linked List
patterns.description: Rewire next pointers directly, reversing or reordering parts of a linked list in place.

patterns.name: Two Heaps
patterns.description: Keep a max-heap for the smaller half and a min-heap for the larger half to track medians and balanced splits.

patterns.name: K-way Merge
patterns.description: Merge several sorted sources at once by repeatedly taking the smallest head from a heap.

patterns.name: Top K Elements
patterns.description: Use a bounded heap (or selection) to keep only the K largest, smallest, or most frequent items.

patterns.name: Modified Binary Search
patterns.description: Adapt binary search to rotated arrays, answer spaces, and monotonic predicates rather than plain sorted lookups.

patterns.name: Subsets
patterns.description: Build every combination or permutation level by level, adding one element at a time.

patterns.name: Greedy Techniques
patterns.description: Make the locally best choice at each step when a proof shows it never hurts the final answer.

patterns.name: Backtracking
patterns.description: Explore choices recursively, undoing each one before trying the next, and prune branches that cannot succeed.

patterns.name: Dynamic Programming
patterns.description: Break a problem into overlapping subproblems and reuse their answers through memoization or tabulation.

patterns.name: Cyclic Sort
patterns.description: Place each number at its own index in one pass when values fall in a known range, exposing missing or duplicate values.

patterns.name: Topological Sort
patterns.description: Order the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points forward, using in-degrees (Kahn) or DFS.

patterns.name: Sort and Search
patterns.description: Sort first so that searching, pairing, or counting becomes a simple scan or binary search.

patterns.name: Matrices
patterns.description: Traverse and transform 2D grids: spirals, rotations, diagonals, and in-place marking.

patterns.name: Stacks
patterns.description: Use a last-in-first-out stack to match brackets, evaluate expressions, and find next greater or smaller elements.

patterns.name: Graphs
patterns.description: Model relationships as nodes and edges, then explore with BFS or DFS, and find shortest paths with Dijkstra and friends.

patterns.name: Tree Depth-First Search
patterns.description: Recurse down a tree depth-first, combining answers from subtrees on the way back up.

patterns.name: Tree Breadth-First Search
patterns.description: Visit a tree level by level with a queue to answer questions about depth, width, and per-level views.

patterns.name: Trie
patterns.description: Store strings character by character in a prefix tree for fast prefix lookups and word searches.

patterns.name: Hash Maps
patterns.description: Trade memory for speed: count, index, and look up values in constant time with hash maps and sets.

patterns.name: Knowing What to Track
patterns.description: Pick the right running state (counts, prefix sums, last-seen positions) so a single pass answers the question.

patterns.name: Union Find
patterns.description: Track connected components with a disjoint-set forest using path compression and union by rank.

patterns.name: Custom Data Structures
patterns.description: Design classes that combine basic structures to meet specific time bounds for each operation.

patterns.name: Bitwise Manipulation
patterns.description: Solve problems with XOR, masks, and shifts by reasoning about individual bits.

patterns.name: Math and Geometry
patterns.description: Apply number theory, geometry, and arithmetic identities to reach a direct formula or a tight simulation.

patterns.name: Challenge Yourself
patterns.description: Mixed problems with no pattern label, so you have to decide which technique fits.
